recipes.name: Chicken Breasts Pierre
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can stewed tomatoes, with liquid

steps.text: In a shallow dish or bowl, combine flour, 1/2 teaspoon salt and ground black pepper. Coat chicken breasts with flour mixture. Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat, and brown chicken on all sides. Remove from skillet, and drain on paper towels.

In the same skillet, combine the tomatoes, water, brown sugar, vinegar and Worcestershire sauce. Season with salt, chili powder, mustard, celery seed, garlic and hot pepper sauce. Bring to a boil; reduce heat, and return chicken to skillet. Cover, and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, or until chicken is tender, no longer pink and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Breasts Pierre
raw_recipe.description: Chicken steeped in a sweet and savory blend of tomatoes, spices and herbs. Serve with crusty French bread to mop up every last drop.

video.description: You’ll return again and again to this simple to prepare and totally delicious chicken dinner. After coating chicken breasts in flour seasoned with salt and pepper, brown in butter. Then simmer in a combination of stewed tomatoes, brown sugar, white vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, chili powder, mustard, celery seed, garlic and hot pepper sauce. Serve with a big hunk of French bread for easy sopping up of that super-good sauce!

review.reviewBody:
This is my kind of dinner! Easy and a unique, yummy flavor. I thought it might be just a bbq sauce; but it is much more... It reminds me a little of Cuban food.
Some of the reviews said this was too sweet. My guess is it was their stewed tomatoes. This was not a real sweet dish with PLAIN DICED CANNED TOMATOES(instead of stewed)like I used. The idea of adding onion (esp. RED onion)sounds, to me, like it would be great; but I don't think mushrooms would work with this(and I love mushrooms). I think, a mix of sliced red onion,and red, yellow and green peppers (in the last 15 min.) steamed in the sauce, would compliment this sauce better; although the recipe is perfect just AS IT IS.
I made with white rice and stir-fried, garlicky, fresh-cracked peppered green beans to make a meal. Although, any starch (noodles, rice etc.) and any green vegetable would be excellent with it. 
It made about a cup of sauce with flavorful chunks of tomato that we spooned over the chicken and rice. I made only four breasts, so I will double sauce for more servings. 'Gotta' have enough of the sauce to add to the rice!
Nancy, you said your husband hasn't gotten sick of this in 15 years... mine liked it a lot too. I have a feeling I will be making for the next 15 years, also. Thank you so much for sharing this one!

So during COVID the slow cooker has become my friend. I took this recipe and adapted easily to a slow cooker. Browned the chicken as in the recipe and then put everything else in the cooker. Added a chicken boullion cube, onions and green pepper as others suggested. Then slow cooked for 5 hours and added some water and corn starch shaken to mix at the end to thicken the sauce. Served over rice. This has incredible flavor. Excellent!!

I read all the reviews and decided to give this a try. Finding something the whole family likes is not always easy. This was a winner! I did as others recommended and used 1/4 cup of white wine and 1/4 cup of water. Also added a few slices of onion and only had chicken tenders. Cooked at low for 1/2 hour. The chicken just melted. My son and husband went back for seconds. This will be a keeper. A big thank you!

Great new dish for the family. A little spicy which the kids loved and hubby sort of loved. I sliced up an onion during the simmer phase and it seemed to add more dimension to this already awesome dish. Also, we like ‘extra’ gravy to our dishes so I doubled up on the simmer sauce. Served with rice, salad and crusty bread. Lots n lots of flavor. Will be making this again.

Delicious. Added onion and green pepper, and added broccoli on top of the chicken to steam it for the last 5 minutes of cooking and save using another pan. Didn’t have Worcestershire sauce so subbed bbq sauce.

I made this last night and it was a big hit with my guys!! Definitely going into the rotation!! I used diced tomatoes because I didn’t have stewed maybe next time I might try it with stewed but then again maybe not lol just the right amount of sweetness and not too salty!! When cooking the chicken I also sprinkled with onion and garlic powder I also added some Italian seasoning to the flour mixture but not a whole lot it was super good and the chicken was cut with your fork tender! So glad I tried this recipe! Thanks so much for sharing 😀

I made it as written, except for substituting fresh tomatoes from the garden, since I have a ton of them. I puréed them in the blender since the family prefers no chunks of tomatoes. The sauce was wonderful. I wouldn’t change a thing, except maybe to add onion as other reviewers suggested. The chicken was tender and delicious. I served with rice, to soak up the sauce, with a salad on the side. I’ll definitely be making this again.

Yumm! Made this as written with adding sliced onion rings and diced yellow and green peppers. I replace water with red wine and the crowd went nuts! Will make this again for sure, very soon! This would be a great dish to entertain guests too!
Amazing and moist chicken. I laid the browned pieces of chicken on top of cooked noodles in a greased baking pan. Then poured the sauce over all and baked for 30 minutes at 350 degrees F.
I made my own stewed tomatoes from frozen tomatoes I had, added onion and pepper per reviews I read - and I have to say - the chicken is secondary to the sauce - fabulous flavor!

LOVE this recipe. I did make a couple of changes because I was looking to use what I had in the pantry and not shop. I substituted a can of peeled diced tomatoes for the stewed tomatoes. I used a couple of squirts of Sriracha (rooster) sauce because we ran out of hot sauce. Also, I placed the chicken breast halves into a zip bag and smashed them a little with a Mason jar. This will become a regular in our rotations.
Easy and delicious! I overpoured on the Worcestershire sauce this time, so I'll be sure to keep it to 2 T as written in the recipe.

I forgot about this recipe and haven't made it for a few years. We were looking for something different to do with our chicken breast and I found this at the bottom of my saved recipes. We made it a few nights ago and it was delicious! Great recipe! We served it over jasmine rice and had a tomato & cucumber salad on the side. It was so good!

This has been a keeper for over 7 years now for my family. The flavors are great for my family's palate. I was able to add more spiciness as my youngest got older. It's so quick and easy fry the ckicken then add to plate make sauce add chicken leave it alone for half hour. I've made this for family and friends, pot lucks it's always the talk cause it's different. I've even changed the recipe a bit to make a wing sauce out of it. I have to thank you for this, cause my family loves it. I even have it written down with pen and paper so I'll never lose it.
Very odd flavor combination. I threw away the leftovers. Substituted red wine for water and added some onions, but otherwise followed the recipe. Just strange.
Very good recipe. Will definitely make this again.
Great recipe! Easy to prepare. Very flavorful. Definitely a keeper.
No changes made. Everybody who tries loves it! One of our friends HATES stewed tomatoes and loved this! Thank you!
